user_prompt: For AMAZON COM INC, did NetIncomeLoss grow year-over-year from FY2024 to FY2025 according to the record's own reported figures?
scope: The single embedded REAL SEC XBRL record AMZN-NetIncomeLoss-FY2025-YoY (top-level records.AMZN-NetIncomeLoss-FY2025-YoY of this instance file), fetched verbatim via bench/fetch_edgar.py from https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts/CIK0001018724.json (PROVENANCE in artifacts/fin-amzn/PROVENANCE, full untrimmed concept history in artifacts/fin-amzn/companyfacts_trimmed.json; restructured from SEC's own list-of-annual-entries shape into flat named keys, see module docstring), read exclusively via inspect_record(record_id='AMZN-NetIncomeLoss-FY2025-YoY', field_path=...): entityName (filer identity), fy_prior.val/fy/fp/form/concept (the FY2024 PRIOR-year annual figure) and fy_current.val/fy/fp/form/concept (the FY2025 CURRENT-year annual figure) -- 'val' is the literal leaf field name in BOTH (e.g. field_path='fy_current.val' reads the current-year number, field_path='fy_prior.val' reads the prior-year number) -- both Form 10-K, as SEC's own structured filer disclosure reports them. The verdict is scoped to whether the record's OWN two per-year figures show the current figure at or above the prior figure -- not to any external analyst consensus or restated/pro-forma figure; no external market-data lookup or human/LLM judgment is used or available; every atom is a closed, mechanically-decidable Boolean predicate over the record (prime_runtime/predicates.py). GROWTH-CLAIM DESIGN NOTE: the closed predicate grammar (prime_runtime/predicates.py) only compares ONE field's value against a FIXED, author-supplied constant -- it cannot directly express a field-vs-field ('current >= prior') comparison. This instance keeps the YoY comparison fully decidable anyway by embedding BOTH fiscal years' values as separate named fields (fy_prior/fy_current) and setting atom E5's numeric_ge THRESHOLD to the prior year's own real value (established exactly by atom E4): E5 then evaluates 'current_value >= prior_value' via the ordinary numeric_ge predicate, mechanically, over the actual field the tool reads at run time -- the model never has to compute or guess the comparison itself, and the runtime never trusts a self-report.

claims.text: The record's filer identity and the existence of a reported NetIncomeLoss figure for FY2025 (current) are located in the supplied record.
The identifying/existence facts are established (C1) and the record's NetIncomeLoss figure for FY2025 is confirmed to equal exactly $77,670,000,000.

Under the supplied record, the FY2024 NetIncomeLoss figure ($59,248,000,000) and the FY2025 figure ($77,670,000,000) are both established from the record's own two per-year entries, and the FY2025 figure meets or exceeds the FY2024 figure: the record's own year-over-year comparison supports the claim that NetIncomeLoss grew from FY2024 to FY2025.

atoms.proposition: The record's filer identity is read via inspect_record(field_path='entityName') and found present.
The record's NetIncomeLoss figure for FY2025 (the current fiscal year) is read via inspect_record(field_path='fy_current.val') and found present.
The same current-FY NetIncomeLoss figure is read again and found to equal exactly $77,670,000,000.

The record's NetIncomeLoss figure for FY2024 (the prior fiscal year, a DISJOINT top-level field from E2/E3's current-FY entry) is read via inspect_record(field_path='fy_prior.val') and found to equal exactly $59,248,000,000.

The current-FY NetIncomeLoss figure is read a third time and evaluated against the PRIOR fiscal year's own reported value ($59,248,000,000, established by E4) as the threshold: found to meet-or-exceed the prior-year figure -- this is the record's OWN year-over-year comparison, decided mechanically by the closed grammar's numeric_ge predicate over the two embedded per-year fields, not by any separate arithmetic step.
Non-route background: the filing form type backing the current-FY figure is read and found to be '10-K' -- not required for, and not evidence toward, the Amazon's net income grew claim.
